items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: And he used to come up there. And when I was going to take intermission, go out and sit down in my chair and take my trumpet

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. How did he play in the old days?

He was an uncle. Really? To me, he was in my time. We used to play up at Beznor's. Had a band up at Beznor's. And before he had to do a trumpet. We used to play up at Olderwise, dancing school. Olderwise. And he used to come up there. And when I was going to take intermission, go out and sit down in my chair and take my trumpet and pull with it like that. All of a sudden, he was like, I don't know how to play it. He did good, too. Oh, yeah. I see. He fusses. He said he writes articles and I think he misses all of…
Yes, I know. He sometimes claims that he originated all of the jazz. Oh, I know.
